author: Daniele Morais
title: Magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes near Honchō (Japan)
subtitle: The quake was recorded at a depth of 43 km, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).
excerpt: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake was recorded near Honchō (Japan), at a depth of 43 km, according to the USGS.
contentHtml:
A magnitude 6.0 earthquake was recorded on August 23, 2026 at 10:44 AM (Brasília time) near Honchō (Japan), according to the United States Geological Survey (USGS). The quake occurred at a depth of roughly 43 km.

What this magnitude means

Earthquakes between magnitude 6 and 7 are considered strong and are usually felt hundreds of kilometers from the epicenter.

What to expect in the coming days

After a main shock, aftershocks — smaller quakes in the same region — are expected over the following days and weeks, with frequency decreasing over time, a well-established pattern in seismology.

With data from the USGS (United States Geological Survey).
